CALL TO ORDER
Chairman Butts called the September 15, 2026 regular meeting of the Baldwin County Board of
Commissioners meeting to order at 6:00 PM.

INVOCATION
Apostle Jackie Farley of Christ Temple of Refuge opened the meeting with a prayer.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
Commissioner Strickland led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Commissioner Strickland made a motion to approve the September 1, 2026 regular meeting and
executive session minutes. Commissioner Davis seconded the motion and the motion passed
unanimously.

Commissioner Little recognized City Councilwoman Arlene Simmons as attending the meeting.

PRESENTATIONS

Certificate Recognition
Vice Chairman Little read a Certificate of Recognition recognizing volunteer firefighter Al
Haslam in celebration of his 100th Birthday.

Baldwin County Fire Recuse Chief Philip Adams along with Deputy Chief Sherry Kneip
highlighted Mr. Haslam’s many years of invaluable service as a volunteer firefighter outlining the
many changes and improvement he had seen as a volunteer fire fighter over the decades. Chief
Adams presented Mr. Haslam with a plaque to show his, Baldwin County Fire Rescue’s and
Baldwin County’s appreciation for this many years of service to the citizens of Baldwin County.

The Commissioners, Chief, and Deputy Chief joined Mr. Haslam at the podium for the
presentation of the certificate and plaque.

Mr. Haslam thanked the commissioners.

Certificate of Recognition
Commissioner Davis read a Certificate of Recognition in celebration of Marilyn Drake as she
celebrates her 90th birthday. Ms. Drake could not be present at the meeting but Ms. Drake’s
daughter and friend joined the commissioners at the podium to receive the certificate on her
behalf.

Ms. Drake’s daughter thanked the Commissioners and expressed how proud her mother was to
have been a teacher in Baldwin County.

Legislative Update
ACCG's Bill Twomey gave an update on the legislative bills that had been introduced in the
Georgia State Legislature and were taking effect. Mt. Twomey discussed:
HB 651 – required school zone cameras to be preceded by flashing yellow lights,
HP 999 – expanded the Magistrate Court jurisdiction capped be raised from $15,000 to $25,000,
HR 1243 – for Next Gen 911 - if approved would go to referendum and would establish the
Georgia 911 fund and it was not clear how those funds would be doled out, the $1.50 fee may not
come directly to the county,
SB 285 – Insurance Premium Tax – the County would have to remit 1.5 % back into the Peace
Officers Fund,
HB 244 – granted 90-day extensions for audits with cause,
HB 1261 – offered Freeport Exemption for electric utilities,
HB 295 – required local governments to compensate property owners when the local
government fails to enforce provisions of law such a loitering and panhandling,
SB 447 – tightened the window for permitting of soil erosion and sediment control,
HB 549 – extended peace officer’s time frame in which training expenses must be reimbursed to
a jurisdiction from 15 months to 36 months,



                                                                                       Page 2 of 5        4

Item 1.




SB 399 – would requiring GEMA to designate the local EMS director as the point of contact and
responsible for the reporting of all AEDs under government issue in government buildings.

Commissioner Strickland asked Mr. Twomey to explain what happened to LHOST in the
special session of the legislature this year.

Mr. Twomey discussed the LHOST and FLOST. He stated LHOST was a version of millage rate
rollback that targeted homeowners directly with homestead exemptions. FLOST was a rollback
in the millage rate that targeted all parcels business would get a tax break as well.

There were quite a few LHOST initiatives and none of them passed.

The Commissioners thanked Mr. Twomey.


ADMINISTRATIVE/FISCAL MATTERS

OLD BUSINESS
Commissioner Davis stated she was getting calls about trash and specifically about the
Meriwether Convenience Center – it was not being cleaned up and people were not able to
dump there. She also stated that previously there were steps to assist people in throwing trash
into the bins. A representative from Ryland responded that there was an attended to help
people with their trash and would check on the Meriwether Convenience Center.

NEW BUSINESS
There was no new business

COUNTY MANAGER'S REPORT
There was no County Manager’s Report

PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD FOR NON-AGENDA ITEMS

Patricia Lane addressed the Commissioners asking which of he Commissioners had an
education and asked if they had been on the Southside. She discussed the poor state of property
and infrastructure in the Black community – it was sad that black people had to live that way.
She discussed public transit being cancelled and asked why the Commissioners lied.

Trisha Clark addressed to Commissioners stating she thought they were going to talk about the
property tax increase. Chairman Butts informed Ms. Clark of when the millage rate public
hearings would take place. She stated she could not afford to have her house note go up and
asked how was it fair to for the citizen to pay back a $15 million loan. She stated that she would
like to have transparency. She stated people would lose their homes because people mishandled
money.



                                                                                       Page 3 of 5        5

Item 1.




Pam Peacock addressed the Commissioners expressing her concern about the County finances,
lack of contracts, lack of accountability and oversight. She stated the County needed to get back
to sound accounting principles, financial control and transparency; the Commissioners needed
to stop using borrowing as a substitute for solving financial problems. She stated the County
should distribute costs to the City of Milledgeville which included the airport and animal
control. She stated the County should petition the State of Georgia for assistance with state
owned property in the County. She stated that raising taxes was not the solution to every
financial problem; raising the millage rate would place a significant financial burden on the
property owners.

Marvin Thigpen addressed the Commissioners expressing his concerns about the deficit and a
tax increase. He stated that he and his wife were on a fixed income and a tax increase would
hurt them very much. Mr. Thigpen stated he wanted transparency and an audit to determine
where the money went and then they needed to prosecute. He stated they needed to find some
way to clear the situation up, the Commissioner made a laughing stock of Baldwin County.

Luke Opperman addressed the Commission asking the Commissioners to take a longer view.
There had been concerns about land use; people needed to have a say in how Baldwin County
developed. He stated they needed a budget the Commissioners understood. He stated that he
hoped they would make a long-term plan beyond reacting to this emergency.

Cindy Humphrey thanked the Commissioners for making repairs to the ditch in front of her
house, even though it took a year and a half. She stated she wanted the meeting to end on a good
note and thanked the Commissioners again.

EXECUTIVE SESSION
Commissioner Little made a motion to go into executive session to discuss real estate matters.
Commissioner Davis seconded the motion and the motion passed unanimously.

The Commissioners went into closed session at 6:44 PM.

Commissioner Strickland made a motion to adjourn the closed session and return to open
